evaluations.title: Constant step-function baseline
evaluations.author: System
evaluations.abstract: A simple constant nonnegative step function supplied as a valid format seed.

evaluations.title: Power-law Asymmetric Singularity Sweep
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact discretization of the continuous power-law density f(x) = (x+0.25)^(-alpha) over 64 values of alpha in [0.05, 0.95]. This tests the hypothesis that asymmetric densities with a boundary singularity perfectly flatten the autoconvolution, preventing central peaks.

evaluations.title: Base JAX Optimizer for Emergent Shapes
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a batched JAX optimizer to maximize the exact Q(f) via gradient descent from random initializations, exploring emergent function shapes.

evaluations.title: Truncated inverse-sqrt kernel: flat-plateau autoconvolution
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the analytic hypothesis that a truncated x^(-1/2) kernel yields an autoconvolution with a flat plateau (Beta identity B(1/2,1/2)=pi) and thus Q well above the 2/3 triangle baseline. Measure exact Q on the evaluator's discretization, its convergence in n, and compare power-law exponents and a two-edge symmetric variant.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained JAX Optimization of Q(f)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Uses JAX and Adam to directly maximize the Q(f) objective over a batch of 64 randomly initialized step functions with N=128 bins. This unbiased search tests whether gradient descent naturally converges to the asymmetric singularity hypothesis or finds novel structural shapes.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Parameterization and Shape Analysis
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Enforces strict symmetry in the JAX optimizer to compare against the unconstrained asymmetric baseline, and generates ASCII plots of the previous winner.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Refinement of Asymmetric Spike-Shoulder Basin
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the best candidate from Eval 5 (N=128), upsamples it to N=2048, and fine-tunes it using JAX and Adam. This tests whether the spike-trough-shoulder structure discovered by unconstrained search becomes significantly sharper and higher-scoring at higher resolutions.

evaluations.title: Optimizer as instrument: local-optimality test and basin discovery for Q
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Use projected gradient ascent (JAX autodiff, with a smoothed-max surrogate for the L-infinity term, then exact polishing) and random restarts to (1) test whether the truncated x^(-1/2) construction Q~0.8812 is a local optimum of Q(w), and (2) discover whether any structurally different basin beats it. Reverse-engineer the shape of any winner.

evaluations.title: Tail-lifting constructions: widening the flat plateau of the autoconvolution
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: The single-edge x^(-1/2) autoconvolution is flat then decays; the ceiling-gap lives in the decaying tail (~21% mass). Test whether superposing shifted/scaled inverse-sqrt kernels or multiplying by a slowly increasing correction lifts the tail toward the plateau ceiling, widening the effective flat region and raising Q above 0.8812.

evaluations.title: Endpoint square-root and power-law survey
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact scoring/diagnostic harness in storage/itera and test one-sided inverse-square-root, power-law, beta-like, and truncated endpoint families. The goal is to verify whether the polynomial square-root boundary-compensation mechanism produces flatter autoconvolution profiles than the constant baseline, while saving candidates and diagnostics for later work.

evaluations.title: Exact scorer and broad mechanism survey
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Build reusable evaluator-compatible scoring and diagnostic utilities, then run a broad deterministic survey of interpretable construction families for the autoconvolution ratio. The goal is to identify which mechanisms can beat the constant baseline and save distinct candidate seeds plus diagnostics for future work.

evaluations.title: Finite atom and block tiling optimizer
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Run an independent high-risk search over finite atom/block mixture representations to test whether pair-sum patch tiling can flatten the autoconvolution better than interval-like profiles. The evaluation should return only structurally distinct candidates and report whether any improvement arises from broad plateau formation rather than isolated spikes.

evaluations.title: Structural Seeding: Landscape Mapping via Diverse Initializations
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Initializes a 64-candidate batch with four distinct structural families (Random, Power-Law Boundary, Chirp, Fractal) to map non-convex phase basins.

evaluations.title: Power-law Asymptotic Limit and Alpha Refinement
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact discrete integration of f(x) = (x+0.25)^(-alpha) at high resolution (N=65536) to sweep alpha continuously between 0.46 and 0.49. This establishes a rigorous analytical limit for the single-parameter power-law family.

evaluations.title: Spike-Shoulder Structural Mask Ablation and Diagnostics
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that exact zeros in the trough improve the spike-shoulder structure by comparing masked optimization against unmasked continuation of the Eval 7 winner.

evaluations.title: Multi-start shape survey + reusable JAX Q-engine (n=256)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable, exact Q-evaluator with autodiff gradient (validated against the constant-f baseline Q=2/3), then run a broad multi-start gradient-ascent survey over structurally diverse initializations at n=256 to map the basin landscape of Q(f)=||f*f||_2^2/(||f*f||_1*||f*f||_inf). Deliver the best Q found, the winning f and g shapes, a trapezoid-based effective-width diagnostic, loss localization, and a basin-diversity clustering.

evaluations.title: Local refinement of asymmetric atom basin
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the robust asymmetric atom/block basin discovered in Eval #12, using its saved top parameters as seeds while preserving diversity and reporting whether the basin remains one-sided, smoothable, and resolution-stable.

evaluations.title: One-sided profile extraction and pair-space diagnostics
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #12 asymmetric winner as a pair-space diagonal projection, then test whether simpler one-sided smooth or soft-niche generators can reproduce the mechanism. This aims to convert a high-scoring optimized seed into a reusable representation.

evaluations.title: Square-root tail-lift correction survey
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Starting from the successful Eval #10 square-root coefficient construction, test asymmetric positive modifications intended to preserve the exact flat prefix while lifting the middle/late convolution tail. The experiment compares simple tail multipliers, small reversed-square-root mixtures, and low-dimensional positive spline multipliers, with diagnostics focused on whether tail lifting improves Q or only creates new peaks.

evaluations.title: Optimizer microscope seeded by square-root profiles
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run a moderate-dimensional optimizer from diverse initializations to learn whether local optimization refines the square-root construction, discovers a distinct motif, or merely creates finite-grid artifacts. The output should include clustered profile diagnostics and transfer checks rather than only the best score.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Scaling and Surrogate Annealing
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Scales N to 1024. Half the batch bootstraps from the upsampled Eval 13 winner, half uses random noise. Implements a temperature-annealed smooth max for the L_infinity surrogate to aggressively flatten the autoconvolution.

evaluations.title: Realizability frontier: target-matching + signed-relaxation price of nonnegativity (n=512)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test directly how flat a nonnegative autoconvolution g=f*f can be by fitting f>=0 to boxcar-like target profiles of varying transition width, tracing the achievable Q envelope. In parallel, solve the UNCONSTRAINED (signed) least-squares deconvolution for the same targets to quantify how much negativity the ideal solution needs, isolating where the nonnegativity constraint binds (edges vs interior). This maps the realizable frontier and the 'price of nonnegativity'.

evaluations.title: Parametric Step-Modulation of Power-Law Singularity
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that modulating the power-law tail reduces L1 mass without destroying the autoconvolution plateau. Optimizes a low-dimensional piecewise-constant multiplier (M=64) over a high-resolution exact power-law base (N=4096).

evaluations.title: Extreme Resolution (N=16384) Masked Spike-Shoulder Optimization
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the Eval 15 masked winner to N=16384 to observe the asymptotic behavior of the spike-shoulder basin. Uses FFT-based JAX convolution to ensure fast execution.

evaluations.title: Extreme Optimization and Scaling to N=4096
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the resolution to N=4096 and extends the Adam optimization to 50,000 steps, aggressively annealing the L_infinity surrogate to enforce extreme flatness.

evaluations.title: Definitive well-resourced global search for optimal Q at n=2048
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Run a well-resourced global optimization of Q(w) at fixed n=2048 (fast exact convolution, near-continuum) using long projected-gradient with fine max-annealing plus exact polish, ~40 diverse restarts, and a CMA-ES/basin-hopping global pass. Definitively test whether any construction beats the truncated inverse-sqrt value at this resolution and characterize the best optimum's shape.

evaluations.title: Generating-function flatness: flattest square of a nonnegative-coefficient sequence
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Reframe the task via generating functions: step-function weights are the nonnegative coefficients of A(z), and the autoconvolution is the coefficient sequence of A(z)^2. Directly optimize nonnegative coefficient sequences for flatness of the squared sequence (the discrete autoconvolution) using a flatness objective, and compare the resulting structures and Q to the discretized inverse-sqrt. Goal: test whether a structurally distinct construction beats or matches 0.8812 and reveals a new mechanism.

evaluations.title: Finite nonnegative polynomial-root target design
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test finite target-profile designs for nonnegative self-convolution roots, starting from the square-root recurrence that gives a flat prefix. The goal is to determine whether tapered or constrained target sequences can reduce the square-root construction's second-half tail without creating a new maximum peak.

evaluations.title: Constrained multi-resolution square-root optimizer
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize low-dimensional smooth corrections around the square-root construction using a multi-resolution objective and explicit penalties against central max relocation. This tests whether the nontransferable n=512 optimizer improvement from Eval #20 can be converted into a robust high-resolution tail correction.

evaluations.title: Continuous optimization of endpoint-tail family
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize the low-dimensional one-sided endpoint-tail family discovered in Eval #18 with continuous/local search and robustness diagnostics. This tests whether the extracted representation is genuinely non-converged and can improve beyond 0.824559 without relying on atom/block seed copying.

evaluations.title: Smooth endpoint-tail plus structured residual equalizer
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the refined block basin can be compressed into an interpretable hybrid: a smooth one-sided endpoint-tail base plus a small number of structured residual niches guided by diagonal deficits and bump-influence diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Understanding & strengthening the asymmetric oscillatory high-Q basin (n=256,1024)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Exp16 found an asymmetric oscillatory f giving Q=0.870, far above the symmetric ceiling (0.724). Investigate the mechanism: is the winning f chirp-like (instantaneous frequency structure), and does its autoconvolution g exhibit an equiripple plateau hugging its maximum? Strengthen the basin with heavy refinement to push Q higher, test explicit chirp-family seeds, and rigorously probe whether asymmetry is essential via a large dedicated symmetric search.

evaluations.title: Scaling law Q*(n): does finer discretization raise the achievable ratio?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Measure how the best achievable Q scales with step count n. If the high-Q mechanism relies on oscillations/ripples in the autoconvolution plateau or on sharper edges, finer n should allow higher Q. Refine the best known basin across n from 128 to ~8192 and, at each n, also run fresh oscillatory starts, recording Q*(n). Fit the trend to determine whether Q saturates or continues rising, and estimate any limiting value.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Spike Geometry and Delta-Probe Ablation
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the geometry of the initial spike in the Eval 15 winner (N=2048) and ablates it by replacing the entire spike with a single non-zero bin (delta function) to test if the spike is structurally just a probe.

evaluations.title: Asymptotic Scaling to N=16384
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Scales resolution to N=16384 with 80,000 optimization steps. Relies on random initialization, which outperformed upsampling in the previous run, to observe the asymptotic shape.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Projected Adam Search (Dynamic Zeros)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an unconstrained search at N=1024 from random initialization. Replaces the unstable exponential parameterization with Projected Adam directly on linear weights (ReLU + max-normalization) to allow exact zeros to form naturally and discover new structural basins.

evaluations.title: Projected Adam Fine-Tuning of Spike-Shoulder Basin
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Fine-tunes the Eval 15 winner at N=8192 using Projected Adam on linear weights. Tests if removing the exponential parameterization allows the multi-lobed spike and zero-trough to sharpen stably without the NaN stalling observed in earlier attempts.

evaluations.title: Prefix-flat generating-function series: high-n SOTA and tail-shaping freedom
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Establish the exact prefix-flat series (coefficients of (1-z)^(-1/2)) as a clean high-resolution construction and test whether the generating-function coefficient freedom can shape the decaying tail. Confirm Q convergence at high n and explore forcing only the first m<n convolution coefficients flat while optimizing the remaining weights to improve the tail and thus Q.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric two-edge kernel: attempting to break the half-support plateau barrier
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: A single left-edge x^(-1/2) singularity produces an autoconvolution plateau over exactly half the support. Analysis suggests the plateau drops past the midpoint because the shrinking overlap window excludes f's heavy left edge. Test whether an ASYMMETRIC two-edge kernel f(x)=x^(-1/2)(w-x)^(-beta) with 0<beta<1/2 (a weaker right-edge singularity) compensates the lost left mass to extend the plateau past 0.5 and raise Q, distinct from the failed symmetric arcsine (beta=1/2) and pure left-edge (beta=0).

evaluations.title: Edge-transition width: what limits it and can endpoint enhancement break Q=0.905?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Scaling shows Q saturates near 0.905 with an equiripple-flat plateau, so ~97.5% of the loss is the edge transition (effective width d_eff≈0.22). This experiment attacks the edge directly: decompose the loss into edge vs plateau precisely, characterize how the current optimum's f behaves near its support endpoints, and test whether enhancing endpoint mass (steps, power-law growth, or a hybrid oscillatory-bulk × edge-envelope parametrization) sharpens g's edges and pushes Q above 0.905. High-risk: the edge width may be fundamentally bounded for nonnegative autoconvolutions.

evaluations.title: Is Q=0.905 a unique basin, and is it the min-peak (Erdos autoconvolution) solution?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Two questions about the ~0.905 optimum. (1) Uniqueness: are there structurally distinct nonnegative step functions achieving Q near 0.905, or is it one dominant basin (up to the reflection/gauge symmetry)? Run many diverse restarts and cluster properly. (2) Connection: on this bounded support, is maximizing Q effectively the same as minimizing ||f*f||_inf at fixed mass (the Erdos-type autoconvolution problem)? Directly minimize the peak at fixed mass, measure the resulting Q, and compare its shape to the Q-maximizer.

evaluations.title: Finite-n optimizer escalation and resolution scan
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Escalate the Eval #20 finite-n optimizer result by optimizing official score directly across several fixed step counts. This treats the n=512 improvement as a valid finite-step basin and tests whether longer, scheduled, multi-start optimization can improve it while characterizing whether the resulting profiles are stable motifs or grid-specific artifacts.

evaluations.title: Block and lobe tiling mechanism survey
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test a structurally distinct representation: f as weighted blocks whose pairwise sum lobes tile the autoconvolution profile. The goal is to see whether ancestry-aware block/lobe superposition can produce high Q or reveal useful failure signatures such as cross-term peaks and holes.

evaluations.title: Endpoint-tail phase 2 precision search
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the now-leading one-sided endpoint-tail representation from Eval #30 with a more precise bounded continuous search, parameter ablations, and high-resolution robustness checks. The aim is to test nonconvergence and identify which features of the profile are necessary.

evaluations.title: Residual equalizer on optimized endpoint-tail base
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the structured residual/equalizer idea to the optimized Eval #30 endpoint-tail base instead of the older Eval #18 base. This tests whether small smooth residuals can improve the current leading representation or whether the smooth endpoint-tail profile is already locally sufficient.

evaluations.title: Inverse diagonal equalizer from endpoint-tail base
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Develop a pair-space/diagonal equalization generator initialized from the leading endpoint-tail profile, using additive nonnegative basis edits selected by their predicted effect on normalized autoconvolution deficits. This tests a representation-level alternative to direct endpoint-tail parameter polishing.

evaluations.title: Upsampling Polish of the Dominant Basin to N=16384
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the winning N=4096 candidate from Eval 25 to N=16384, applies varying levels of noise, and optimizes for 80,000 steps to polish the optimal shape.

evaluations.title: Clean Projected Adam Continuation (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the Eval 15 winner to N=4096 and fine-tunes using Projected Adam with zero/microscopic noise to prevent structural disruption.

evaluations.title: Greedy Coordinate Local Search (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Applies a discrete, gradient-free greedy coordinate descent to the Eval 15 winner to explicitly test if combinatorial modifications (forcing exact zeroes) can escape gradient stalling.

evaluations.title: Direct continuation of Eval 42 high-score basin
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the Eval #42 high-score basin directly at n=4096 and nearby higher resolutions. Eval #42 found a stable 0.902078 motif without directly optimizing n=4096; this run starts from its winner and close cluster representatives, uses best-checkpoint tracking, and tests whether the basin has remaining headroom.

evaluations.title: Eval 42 motif extraction and parametric fit
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Extract an interpretable reusable description of the Eval #42 high-score motif. Fit low-dimensional smooth/bump parameterizations to the winner, analyze its autoconvolution peak ancestry, and test whether the fitted formula reproduces the 0.902 motif across resolutions.

evaluations.title: The positive-definiteness obstruction: why symmetric f caps Q and asymmetry escapes it
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: A candidate mechanism explaining the large symmetric-vs-asymmetric gap (0.724 vs 0.905): for symmetric f, f-hat is real so g-hat = f-hat^2 >= 0, making g positive-definite (Bochner); a positive-definite g attains its max at the origin and cannot be flat-topped, since a boxcar has sign-changing Fourier coefficients. Asymmetric f has complex f-hat, so g-hat = f-hat^2 is not sign-constrained and g can approach a box. This experiment tests the sign structure of g-hat for the symmetric vs asymmetric optima, robustly re-measures the symmetric ceiling, and probes whether ~0.724 is the best-achievable positive-definite (symmetric) value.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric edge structure: sharp leading edge, long trailing edge, and the endpoint-profile reduction
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval40 revealed the optimal g is asymmetric with one narrow edge (~0.09) and one broad edge (~0.40). Characterize this asymmetry cleanly and test the reduction that each edge of g equals the one-sided autoconvolution of f's inward endpoint profile. Determine whether the sharp-edge/broad-edge split is a robust feature of the optimum and how it relates to the equiripple plateau and the 0.905 value.

evaluations.title: Inverse design toward a full box: realizability limits of near-indicator self-convolutions
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Prior work made the autoconvolution flat on a LEFT prefix (half the support), capping Q at ~0.8825. This experiment inverts the design: given a target g that is a near-full indicator (flat on [delta,1-delta] with thin ramps) or a centered trapezoid, find the best nonnegative f whose self-convolution approximates it via nonnegative-constrained deconvolution, then measure the achieved Q and the realizability gap. Directly probes how close a nonnegative self-convolution can get to a complete box and whether any target beats the single-edge 0.8825 ceiling.

evaluations.title: Pruned residual hybrid refinement and mechanism split
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the Eval #45 residual hybrid lead while explicitly testing whether gains come from broadening the main high-convolution region or from a pruned/narrow-maximum regime. Use the reported unreturned ablation as a control, then reoptimize residual count, amplitudes, and base parameters with robustness diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Phase Retrieval via Alternating Projections (Gerchberg-Saxton)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Explores a completely different mathematical paradigm: using alternating projections between the frequency domain (target sinc magnitude) and time domain (positivity, bounded support) to synthesize flat autoconvolutions.

evaluations.title: Greedy Coordinate Local Search Continuation (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the successful Eval 49 greedy search winner to N=4096 and runs a finer-grained greedy coordinate descent to test if discrete optimization scales better than Adam at high resolution.

evaluations.title: Direct Fractal IFS via Kronecker Cascades
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a small base vector of length k and uses Kronecker products to deterministically construct a perfectly self-similar fractal step function at high resolutions.

evaluations.title: Multi-resolution diverse-init direct-Q search: testing dome, bimodal, and fine-structure hypotheses
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Prior optimizers were seeded near inverse-sqrt and budget-limited, all converging to Q~0.8825. This experiment runs a from-scratch, multi-resolution direct-Q maximization explicitly seeded AWAY from inverse-sqrt: random nonnegative, symmetric bimodal, and smooth-dome-realization inits, with coarse-to-fine refinement that allows fine/spiky structure to emerge. Tests three hypotheses at once: (A) the optimizer is a smooth non-flat dome, (B) a symmetric bimodal f, (C) hierarchical fine structure. Decisive either way: a beat >0.8825 opens a new basin; reconvergence strengthens the near-optimality evidence.

evaluations.title: Generative test: does one-sharp/one-broad + equiripple structure reproduce Q≈0.905?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the empirically observed structure is GENERATIVE. Construct explicit target g profiles = flat plateau + one sharp edge (small exponent) + one broad edge, sweeping the edge-width ratio and edge exponents, then project each target onto the nearest nonnegative autoconvolution (optimize f>=0 to match). Confirm whether Q peaks near the observed ~4:1 edge ratio and reaches ≈0.905, and whether symmetric two-equal-edge targets fall short. This validates the structural characterization as predictive rather than merely descriptive.

evaluations.title: Can a different search break Q=0.905? Basin-hopping / evolutionary over asymmetric structures
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Guard against mistaking the gradient-descent basin for the global optimum. Use a structurally different global search (basin-hopping and a CMA/evolutionary strategy over compact asymmetric parametrizations, plus large-n aggressive refinement) to test whether any construction exceeds the current record Q≈0.9055. A clear failure to surpass it across diverse methods strengthens (without proving) that ~0.905 is near-optimal; any surpass would open a new basin.

evaluations.title: Unified low-edge equalizer residual search
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Merge the two strongest recent mechanisms: Eval #55 compact low-edge residual hybrids and Eval #46 multiplicative low-edge diagonal equalization. Test whether a unified low-edge reweighting/residual model improves beyond Q=0.86974843 while explaining which edits are essential.

evaluations.title: Compact staged-profile grammar test
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the current high-scoring one-sided hybrids can be compressed into a small staged-profile grammar: prelude, low shoulder, main shoulder/tail, and endpoint accent. This is a representation-level check distinct from residual polishing.

evaluations.title: Second continuation of Eval 50 basin
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the non-converged Eval #50 high-score basin from its 0.9030425996 winner. This run emphasizes longer perturb-refine, direct n=4096 fine tuning, optional n=8192 fine tuning if feasible, and stable high-resolution resampling diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Endpoint-power shoulder model for Eval 50 motif
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Build an interpretable endpoint-power plus localized-shoulder parameterization of the Eval #50 high-score motif. Starting from Eval #51's shoulder coordinates and endpoint exponent, fit/refine shoulder locations, widths, and amplitudes, run ablations, and test whether a reusable moderate-dimensional model can reproduce or improve the 0.903 motif.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: autocorrelation-ratio lower bound and Renyi entropy gap across candidates
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Validate the rigorous structural identities empirically across the candidate bank: confirm ∫g^2 = ∫R^2 (autoconvolution and autocorrelation have equal L2 norm), confirm M = ||f*f||_inf <= ||f||_2^2 = R(0) giving the lower bound Q >= Q_R = ∫R^2/R(0), and compute the Renyi entropy gap H_inf - H2 = -log Q. This produces reusable paper-supporting numerics and a diagnostic tool, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Iterated Function System (IFS) Representation Optimization
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the fractal hypothesis by optimizing a 3-map Iterated Function System (IFS) to generate the weight density, radically reducing dimensionality and enforcing self-similarity.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Frequency Domain Signature of the 0.909 Basin
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the frequency spectrum of the Eval 49 winner to understand why it succeeds and how its phase/magnitude differs from the theoretical sinc target.

evaluations.title: Scale-Invariant Surrogate Polish at N=32768
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the Q=0.9378 winner to N=32768 and optimizes using a numerically stable, scale-invariant L_infinity surrogate to perfectly flatten the phase peaks.

evaluations.title: Continuous low-edge connector refinement
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the current Eval #62 lead by replacing the four compact low-edge residuals with a continuous connector/nested-residual parameterization around x=0.49-0.54. The evaluation tests whether the leading additive prelude mechanism is still nonconverged and whether it can be represented more cleanly than stacked bumps.

evaluations.title: Adaptive positive spline profile search
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Run a broader one-sided positive spline/adaptive-profile search to test whether the low-edge prelude, shoulders, tail, and endpoint accent emerge without hard-coding the residual cluster. This provides a representation-level check against overfitting the current Eval #62 basin.

evaluations.title: High-resolution continuation from Eval 64
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #64 basin from its 0.9035328098 n=16384 winner/resamples. This run tests direct n=8192 or n=16384 low-rate polishing if feasible, otherwise a longer n=4096 polish with robust high-resolution validation.

evaluations.title: Compact-hat local basis refinement of Eval 64 motif
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Use compact localized hat bases, the best compression language from Eval #65, to model and refine the Eval #64 motif. The goal is to learn whether adaptive local bases can reproduce most of the 0.9035 score with fewer degrees of freedom and whether optimizing in this basis can generate useful structured perturbations.

evaluations.title: Continuum-limit confirmation: very-large-n refinement of the record basin
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Solidify the empirical continuum limit by refining the record asymmetric basin at very large n (16384, 32768, 65536) and comparing to the fitted Q_inf≈0.9054 from Eval33. A single coherent refinement pipeline: upsample the best n=1024 solution, continue Adam ascent with FFT convolution, exact-rescore. Determine whether Q keeps its ~1/n approach to ~0.9054 or shows any departure at large n.

evaluations.title: Equioscillation optimality condition: does the plateau alternation characterize the optimum?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test the conjecture that the high-Q optimum is characterized by a Chebyshev-type equioscillation condition on the plateau of g. Precisely measure whether the plateau local maxima truly equalize (touching a common level) at the optimum, whether their number grows with resolution, and whether a KKT/stationarity analysis of Q at the optimum is consistent with ||g||_inf being active at many points. Compare against deliberately perturbed near-optima to see if equalization is the signature of optimality rather than an accident.

evaluations.title: Sparse atom and structured-gap constructions: additive-combinatorics probe
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: All prior constructions used dense/contiguous weights. This probes the genuinely-untested sparse regime: f as optimized discrete atoms (spike positions) and as structured sequences with gaps/periodic zeros, motivated by additive-combinatorics covering ideas. Tests whether a self-convolution can be flatter via sparse-support structure rather than a dense inverse-sqrt profile. Expected (conjecture) to underperform due to the diagonal-vs-offdiagonal weight asymmetry, but this is the last uncovered construction family and closes the search honestly.

evaluations.title: Ultimate Asymptote: Scaling to N=98304
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the Q=0.9397 winner to N=98304, nearing the 100,000 task limit, and polishes it with the scale-invariant surrogate for 60,000 steps.

evaluations.title: Continuous Sparse Point-Mass Optimization (K-Sparse Comb)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the density as a sparse combination of exactly K discrete uniform pulses (weights=1). Optimizes the continuous locations of these K pulses to maximize Q(f), bypassing bin-weight gradient vanishing by optimizing positions directly.

evaluations.title: Variational influence map around current lead
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Eval #70 current lead by computing directional influence maps for additions, removals, multiplicative gates, and local reparameterizations. Use the map to test a small number of predicted nonlocal edits rather than continuing blind low-edge polishing.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical staged prelude construction
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test a distinct multiscale construction in which the one-sided prelude/shoulder/tail/endpoint pattern is generated recursively or by nested motifs rather than fitted residual stacks. This probes whether the current low-edge mechanism has a scalable hierarchical analogue.

evaluations.title: Definitive prefix-flat SOTA at maximum resolution and continuum-limit extrapolation
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Establish the definitive best Q for the prefix-flat (1-z)^(-1/2) construction at the evaluator's maximum practical resolution (n up to 100000) and extrapolate the continuum limit. This fixes the SOTA number and convergence rate for publication.

evaluations.title: Converged optimization: explicit L-infinity handling to certify the true optimum
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval75 showed the Adam 'record' is not stationary: a single linearized peak-lowering step improved Q, and the projected gradient RMS was ~0.034. The nonsmooth max(g) denominator makes plain Adam under-converge. Build an optimizer that handles the L-infinity term explicitly (scale-fixed constrained formulation with iterated peak-lowering / minimax refinement) and drive solutions to certified stationarity at n=1024 and 4096. Report the converged Q, a convergence certificate (projected-gradient / active-set structure), and re-characterize the converged optimum's plateau and edges.

evaluations.title: Certified upper bound for symmetric (positive-definite) constructions via convex duality
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The symmetric case is provably positive-definite (g-hat = f-hat^2 >= 0) with max at center, and numerically caps near Q=0.724. Attempt to turn this cap into a rigorous certified upper bound: relax to the class of nonnegative positive-definite g supported on [-1/2,1/2] with g(0)=max=1, and compute a certified upper bound on ∫g^2/∫g over this relaxed (convex-friendly) class via a linear/semidefinite programming dual. A valid finite bound strictly below the asymmetric record would rigorously establish that asymmetry is necessary. High-risk: the relaxation or dual may be loose or intractable.

evaluations.title: Projected Adam with Hard L_infinity Penalty
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Fine-tunes the Eval 49 winner (N=2048) by adding a strong penalty term to the Q(f) objective to actively suppress the L_infinity peak, forcing the optimizer to flatten the autoconvolution and escape the local optimum.

evaluations.title: Ultra-polish continuation from Eval 72
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the current best Eval #72 high-resolution basin from its 0.9035535559 winner. This run focuses on low-rate n=8192 polishing, longer n=16384 follow-up if useful, and convergence diagnostics to decide whether continued exploitation remains productive.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical adaptive local-basis model for Eval 72 motif
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the compact-hat representation from Eval #73 into a hierarchical adaptive local basis for the Eval #72 motif. The run tests whether endpoint-locked, group-aware local bases with more degrees can close the gap to the full vector and provide an interpretable compression map.

evaluations.title: Exact finite-n optimum of Q for small n: rigorous near-optimality benchmark
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: For small step counts n=2..8 the weight space is low-dimensional enough that heavy multi-start optimization yields near-certain global optima of Q. Establish the exact optimal Q(n) for small n, compare to the inverse-sqrt/prefix-flat construction at the same n, and examine whether small-n optima are already inverse-sqrt-like. This provides a rigorous finite-n near-optimality benchmark for the construction, distinct from continuum heuristics.

evaluations.title: Low-Degree B-Spline Envelope Optimization
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the density f(x) using a low-degree B-spline with a small number of control points (K=24). This tests if a strictly smooth, low-dimensional envelope can discover a high-scoring basin without the high-frequency jaggedness of previous runs.

evaluations.title: Helix candidate registry and reconstruction toolkit
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the Helix lineage's scattered autoconvolution artifacts into a reusable candidate registry and reconstruction toolkit, including representative candidates from each discovered basin, exact scores, robustness checks, parameters, diagnostics, and recommended next actions.

evaluations.title: Finite-basis local saturation and nonlocal edit scan
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Use the current Eval #79/Eval #70 lead to run a broader finite-basis local saturation scan across additive, multiplicative, attenuation, and component-shift directions. The goal is to identify nonlocal edit opportunities or provide a scoped finite-basis saturation map, not to do another narrow residual polish.

evaluations.title: Bounded convergence check from Eval 85
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run a deliberately bounded continuation from Eval #85 to test whether the high-score basin has remaining material headroom. Because Eval #85 improved by only 5e-6, this evaluation emphasizes convergence diagnostics and stopping evidence rather than unconstrained score chasing.

evaluations.title: Local-cosine basis optimization around Eval 85 motif
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Use the strong local-cosine compression result from Eval #86 as an explicit optimization coordinate system around the Eval #85 motif. The goal is to see whether a 768-1536 degree local basis can reproduce or improve the high-score vector while preserving interpretability through group structure and ablations.

evaluations.title: Converged scaling law: properly-optimized Q*(n) to settle the continuum question
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: The earlier scaling estimate was under-converged (Eval74 large-n was beaten by a converged n=4096 in Eval82). Re-measure Q*(n) using the converged active-set + peak-lowering optimizer from Eval82 at each n, with a convergence check at every n, to obtain a trustworthy Q*(n) curve and an honest statement about whether Q saturates to a finite continuum limit or keeps rising. This replaces the retracted clean-1/n claim.

evaluations.title: Why does asymmetry help? Decompose Q gains along the symmetry-breaking path
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Establish mechanistically HOW asymmetry raises Q beyond the symmetric cap. Interpolate between a converged symmetric optimum (Q≈0.724) and the converged asymmetric optimum (Q≈0.906) along a path that gradually introduces asymmetry (e.g., via a phase/asymmetry parameter), tracking how the Fourier sign structure of g, the plateau flatness, and the edge asymmetry evolve. Identify the precise structural change that lifts Q: does g acquire negative Fourier components (leaving the positive-definite cone) exactly as Q rises past 0.724?

evaluations.title: Novelty-biased basin search beyond Eval 91
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run a fresh optimizer search designed to avoid simply re-polishing the Eval #91 basin. Use exact-Q optimization with novelty penalties or distance filters from the current best motif, diverse initializations, and transfer checks to look for distinct high-scoring basins or confirm that nearby searches collapse back to the known motif.

evaluations.title: Analytical Pipeline: Spike-Constrained Shoulder Optimization
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Decomposes the density into a fixed delta spike and a trainable shoulder. Optimizes only the shoulder H(x) to flatten the cross-term 2*S*H and the self-term H*H, exploiting the asymmetry of autoconvolution.

evaluations.title: Exact Global Optima at Small N (N=2 to 8)
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Performs massive random restarts for very small N (2 through 8) to find the absolute global optimum, hoping to reveal an exact algebraic pattern in the weights.

evaluations.title: Shoulder-endpoint interaction refinement
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Refine and analyze the shoulder/end-tail edit class discovered in Eval #90: compact low-shoulder additions near x≈0.68-0.70 paired with endpoint-tail spreading near x≈0.88. The goal is to test whether this is a robust mechanism or only a local perturbation.

evaluations.title: Inverse plateau synthesis with staged basis
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Use a plateau/level-set target objective with a staged positive basis to synthesize candidates from less local assumptions. This tests whether low-edge, shoulder, and endpoint-tail features emerge from trying to make h=g/Linf more indicator-like, rather than from perturbing the current lead.

evaluations.title: Self-similar high-score motif tiling survey
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Use the current high-score Eval #91/Eval #85 motif as a reusable component rather than a vector to polish. Render mixtures of translated, scaled, and weighted copies of the motif inside the allowed interval, then diagnose whether self/cross convolution lobes can fill valleys or whether they create new dominant peaks.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Tool: Active Set and Stationarity Suite
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a reusable diagnostic suite in storage/lumina to analyze KKT-like stationarity, active L_infinity constraints, and gradient residuals. Applies it to the Eval 49 winner (N=2048) to reveal the mathematical shape of the spike-shoulder equilibrium.

evaluations.title: Continuous Particle Optimization via Differentiable Splatting
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the step function as K continuous spikes with floating-point positions. Differentiably splats them onto an N=32768 grid to allow spikes to physically glide across gaps.

evaluations.title: Certified symmetric bound via atomic-cosine reformulation + Delsarte-type LP dual
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a rigorous certified upper bound on Q for the symmetric (positive-definite) class using the exact spectral reformulation: for symmetric g with g(0)=1, g(t)=integral cos(2*pi*xi*t) dmu(xi) with mu>=0, and on the support [-1/2,1/2] the objective becomes Q(mu) = [double-integral K dmu dmu] / [integral sinc dmu], with K(xi,eta)=0.5*(sinc(xi-eta)+sinc(xi+eta)) and sinc(xi)=sin(pi*xi)/(pi*xi). Because the numerator is a convex PSD quadratic form, the relaxed optimum is atomic; combine this with the nonnegativity constraint g>=0 via a Delsarte/Beurling-Selberg dual multiplier to certify a bound. Goal: a valid U_sym, ideally < asymmetric record 0.906, proving asymmetry necessary.

evaluations.title: Global-optimality probe: many independent converged starts and structural convergence
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen (not prove) the near-optimality of Q≈0.9064 by running many independent converged optimizations (diverse random and structured starts, each driven to stationarity with the Eval82 active-set + peak-lowering optimizer) at n=1024, and checking whether they all converge to the same Q and the same n-independent structure (d_eff≈0.219, edges 0.090/0.398). Report the distribution of converged Q and whether any distinct basin approaches or exceeds the record.

evaluations.title: Refined compressed-copy punctuation optimization
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the explicit two-copy Eval #99 construction: a compressed/shifted high-score motif plus a tiny boundary punctuation component. Optimize only interpretable copy parameters, validate at high resolution, and test whether the compressed-copy branch can improve beyond 0.9035709659.

evaluations.title: Punctuation-copy mechanism and support-framing analysis
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose why the tiny Eval #99 boundary component helps. This evaluation runs controlled ablations and local parameter probes to determine whether the punctuation copy changes support framing, normalization, tail mass, peak structure, or discretization behavior.

evaluations.title: High-precision verification of the exact continuum value Q = 4 ln 2 / pi
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Directly verify, to high numerical precision, the claimed closed-form continuum value Q_inf = 4 ln 2/pi for the truncated inverse-square-root construction, including the intermediate exact quantities: plateau g=pi on (0,1/2), tail g(t)=4 arcsin sqrt(1/(2t))-pi on (1/2,1), ||g||_1=2, ||g||_inf=pi, and tail integral T=int_{1/2}^1 g^2 = 8 ln 2 - pi^2/2. This secures the paper's centerpiece result.

evaluations.title: Equiripple height-distribution diagnostic and generator
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze Helix representative candidates through a classical approximation lens: level-set distributions, deficit curves, and equiripple-like residuals of h=g/Linf. Then test a small generator that tries to equalize the high-region deficit rather than directly perturbing known residual stacks.

evaluations.title: Quadrature and moment node construction survey
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Explore an older quadrature/moment-design representation: choose a small set of positive nodes/components so that pair-sum diagonal statistics match plateau-like moment or level constraints. Compare these constructions to the current residual-rich lead and staged grammar.

evaluations.title: Exact Extremizer Sequence for Small N
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically solves the exact extremizer for very small N (4, 8, 16, 32) using multi-start L-BFGS-B. This tests if the spike-shoulder structure and exact zeroes emerge natively at low resolutions or if they are finite-resolution artifacts.

evaluations.title: Exact Constrained Optimization via SLSQP (N=64)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Q(f) objective as a constrained optimization problem to handle the non-smooth L_infinity max function correctly. Solves N=64 using SLSQP to find a strict KKT-stationary local optimum.

evaluations.title: Float64 Ultimate Polish at N=98304
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Enables JAX float64 precision and runs a 100,000-step final polish on the Q=0.94056 winner to definitively converge the dominant basin.

evaluations.title: Toolkit update and Helix handoff synthesis
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Update the Helix toolkit and lineage handoff notes with the latest current-best candidate and scoped negative probes, producing a consolidated research map for future descendants before maturity.

evaluations.title: Classical window and spectral-factorization probe
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Probe old-style filter/window representations: one-sided minimum-phase-like windows, equiripple/Chebyshev-inspired windows, prolate/Kaiser-like windows, and spectral square-root heuristics for plateau targets. The goal is a distinct coordinate system or a scoped negative result, not local bump polishing.

evaluations.title: High-resolution robust two-copy refinement
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the Eval #105 explicit two-copy construction using a high-resolution-stability objective across n=16384/32768/65536/100000. The goal is to improve or stabilize the compressed-main plus tiny-punctuation mechanism without full-vector polishing.

evaluations.title: Norm-decomposition theory for punctuation copy
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze why a tiny remote punctuation copy improves the compressed motif. This run computes first-order and finite-difference changes in L1, L2, Linf, h-mass, support, and max location when adding a tiny component, aiming to distinguish support-framing from cross-lobe filling and guide future parameter searches.

evaluations.title: VERIFY the claimed symmetric bound Q <= 4/(3*sqrt(3)): explicit proof and symmetry dependence
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Eval103 reported a rigorous analytic bound Q <= 4/(3*sqrt(3)) ≈ 0.76980 for symmetric realizable f via 'sharp Young's inequality plus interpolation'. This must be verified rigorously before any use. Critically: the asymmetric record is 0.9064 > 0.7698, so if the proof does NOT genuinely use symmetry/positive-definiteness, it is FALSE. Reproduce the full step-by-step proof, identify exactly where symmetry is used, and stress-test it numerically to confirm it is a valid symmetric-only bound (and cannot be an error that also 'bounds' the asymmetric case).

evaluations.title: Smooth LogSumExp Relaxation and L-BFGS (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the non-smooth L_infinity max function with a smooth LogSumExp relaxation. Optimizes the N=2048 Eval 49 winner using JAX-based L-BFGS to gracefully navigate the tied exact-max knots and allow stuck zeroes to grow.

evaluations.title: Direct High-N Search with Scale-Invariant Surrogate
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the corrected scale-invariant surrogate allows direct optimization from random noise at N=16384 to surpass the upsampled basin.

evaluations.title: Current-lead neighborhood map and stopping criteria
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Map the local neighborhood of the Eval #108 current lead across structured edit classes to quantify remaining local opportunity and establish stopping criteria for near-neighbor refinement. This is a diagnostic guardrail against endless small score-chasing.

evaluations.title: Moment and level-distribution theory sketch
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze representative Helix candidates through moment, quantile, and normalized-height distribution summaries to formulate a scoped theory sketch: what properties distinguish high-scoring one-sided residual/equalizer profiles from lower-scoring compressed controls?

evaluations.title: Second robust refinement of reversed-tiny two-copy branch
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the explicit two-copy branch from Eval #115, focusing on the reversed-tiny high-resolution-robust candidate. The search optimizes only main/tiny copy parameters with ranking by stability through n=100000 and constraints against first-order Linf lift.

evaluations.title: Recursive compressed-motif punctuation survey
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #115 two-copy construction can serve as a new base motif for another compressed-copy plus punctuation layer. This evaluates a recursive/framing mechanism while keeping all candidates explicit mixtures of a small number of rendered motif copies.

evaluations.title: Euler-Lagrange stationarity of Q: derive and verify the KKT condition at the converged asymmetric optimum
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Derive the exact first-order (KKT) stationarity condition for the scale-invariant objective Q(f)=||g||_2^2/(||g||_1 ||g||_inf), g=f*f, over nonnegative step functions, and verify it on the converged asymmetric optimum (Eval82/93). Goal: obtain a concrete integral characterization of the optimum that explains the universal structure (d_eff, edge asymmetry, endpoint suppression) and provides a rigorous stationarity certificate distinguishing converged from under-converged solutions.

evaluations.title: Robust two-punctuation refinement from Eval 123
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the explicit multi-punctuation construction found in Eval #123. The goal is to improve native score while also finding a high-resolution robust two-tiny candidate through n=100000, distinguishing true multi-punctuation gains from q100000-fragile variants.

evaluations.title: Toolkit update with Eval120 and theory diagnostics
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Update the Helix toolkit and handoff with the new Eval120 current best and Eval121 level-distribution theory diagnostics, including clear stopping guidance against further unstructured near-neighbor polishing.

evaluations.title: Canonical componentized current-lead representation
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Convert the current Eval120 near-neighbor lead from layered edit history into a canonical named-component representation: endpoint-tail base, low-edge connector, shoulders, endpoint-tail spread, endpoint accent, and attenuation gates. Test how much score is preserved and which components are necessary.

evaluations.title: Active-Set SLSQP on Reduced Knot Set (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Solves the N=2048 spike-shoulder basin as an exact constrained optimization problem using SciPy SLSQP. To prevent O(N^2) memory explosion, only the top M=1000 autoconvolution knots from the base candidate are passed as inequality constraints.

evaluations.title: Archive-readiness synthesis and paper skeleton
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Prepare an archive-readiness synthesis for maturity: a concise paper skeleton, experiment table, novelty questions, and related-work checklist based on Helix artifacts. This is not a publication submission, only preparation for comparing against archive work after tick 40.

evaluations.title: Transport-map representation probe
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test a nonlocal coordinate system: represent f by monotone transport/quantile maps from a simple base density, then optimize transport knots to shape the autoconvolution height distribution. This aims to escape local bump-edit history while retaining one-sided staging.

evaluations.title: Explicit three-punctuation robust search
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Eval #125 explicit two-punctuation branch to up to three tiny punctuation components. The search keeps all candidates as low-parameter rendered mixtures and ranks both native score and high-resolution robustness through n=100000.

evaluations.title: First-order punctuation placement analysis
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Develop a first-order placement diagnostic for tiny punctuation components. For the current main and multi-punctuation branches, compute where an infinitesimal remote component should improve log-Q by increasing L2 without increasing Linf, then compare predictions against known Eval #105/#115/#123/#125 placements.

evaluations.title: Verify the unconditional inequality Q*rho <= 4/(3*sqrt(3)) and characterize the rho=1 equality (symmetry)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Empirically verify the newly-derived unconditional inequality Q(f)*rho(f) <= 4/(3*sqrt(3)) for all nonnegative f, where rho=max(f*f)/int f^2, and confirm the exact equality characterization rho=1 iff f symmetric. This generalizes the symmetric theorem (its rho=1 slice) and makes the necessity of asymmetry precise. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: Certified small-n global optimality of Q via moment-SOS (Lasserre) with interval branch-and-bound fallback
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Upgrade the finite-n optimality claim from heuristic multistart (Eval #87) to a certified statement. For small step counts n, compute certified upper bounds on Q(f) using the moment-SOS (Lasserre) hierarchy, and compare against the prefix-flat lower bound. Where the certified upper bound matches the prefix-flat value within tolerance, global optimality is proven for that n. This is a rigor-upgrade / tool-building evaluation; it returns None (non-scoring).

evaluations.title: Analytical Macro-Template Optimization (Spike-Trough-Polynomial)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the spike-shoulder basin as an 8-parameter analytical template (spike pos/width/amplitude + zero trough + polynomial shoulder) and optimizes it using Differential Evolution at high resolution (N=4096), bypassing all gradient pathologies.

evaluations.title: Gaussian Splatting: Variable-Density Continuous Particles
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Models the function as K=1024 Gaussian particles with trainable positions, amplitudes, and widths to natively discover optimal density vs. sparsity.

evaluations.title: First-order guided robust two-punctuation refinement
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the leading two-punctuation branch using the Eval #132 first-order placement diagnostic as a filter. The search keeps tiny3 disabled, tunes two explicit punctuation components, and ranks native score, q100000, and min-high-resolution objectives separately.

evaluations.title: Robust-objective comparison for punctuation branches
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Compare all leading punctuation candidates under consistent high-resolution objectives and norm decompositions. This creates a clean decision table for native score, q100000, min-highres, and mechanism clarity before maturity/archive access.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Tool: Gray-Mass Loss and Source-Pair Projection
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a reusable diagnostic tool to compute the gray-mass integral 1 - Q = int h(1-h)/int h. Applies it to the Eval 118 winner (N=2048) to map exactly which t-intervals and source pair-sums cause the score loss.

evaluations.title: Contiguous Masking and Continuous Recovery (Basin-Jump)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the contiguous masking topology operator from station guidance. Applies a sliding 20-bin zero-mask across the Eval 118 winner's shoulder and uses JAX/Adam continuous recovery to cross non-smooth barrier ties.

evaluations.title: Frontier calibration: asymmetric high-Q via scale-invariant log-sum-exp surrogate + exact coordinate polish + mask basin-jumps
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Independently reproduce and calibrate the reported >0.93 asymmetric regime for Q(f)=||f*f||_2^2/(||f*f||_1·||f*f||_inf). Use a scale-invariant smooth surrogate (log-sum-exp softmax for the L-infinity term) over w=u^2 to discover an asymmetric envelope, warm-start up a resolution ladder, apply exact-score coordinate polish, and use contiguous zero-masking basin-jumps to escape local optima. Goal: obtain my own frontier construction well above the invsqrt value 0.88254 and characterize its structure. This is a calibration/reproduction run; it returns the best construction as the submission.

evaluations.title: Targeted Gray-Mass Masking and Recovery
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the diagnostic insight from Eval 139 to specifically mask the source bins (1376 to 1536) that project into the worst-performing gray-mass tail t in [0.2, 0.25]. Tests if targeted role-aware pruning allows L-BFGS to jump to a higher basin.

evaluations.title: Topology-masking pilot from robust punctuation parent
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Pilot contiguous masking plus recovery from the strongest robust punctuation parent. This tests the previous-station guidance that topology-altering masks can cross barriers, while preserving exact-score/q100000 diagnostics and comparing against the current punctuation controls.

evaluations.title: Does climbing Q force rho down? Independent topology-mask/warm-start ascent tracing (Q, rho, gray-mass)
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test the explanatory reach of the unconditional inequality Q*rho <= 4/(3*sqrt(3)) (rho=||f*f||_inf/||f||_2^2) against distinct high-Q basins by independently climbing Q with a topology-mask + warm-start-ladder search and tracing the trajectory of (Q, rho, gray-mass fraction, asymmetry). Goal: reach Q well above my 0.9064 basin for calibration, and determine whether higher Q strictly requires lower rho and lower intermediate-height ('gray') mass, connecting the obstruction theory to the frontier ascent mechanism. Analysis-focused; may emit the best distinct construction as a seed.

evaluations.title: Coherence parameter rho across DISTINCT frontier basins: test Q*rho <= 4/(3√3) and rho <= C^4/Q prediction
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Measure the coherence parameter rho=||f*f||_inf/||f||_2^2 and related structure (Q, gray-mass, mass-above-threshold, asymmetry) on the DISTINCT high-Q frontier constructions from multiple lineages (Epsilon Eval#112 Q=0.941, Lumina Eval#118 Q=0.9096, Itera Eval#138 Q=0.9039, my Eval#93/#82 Q=0.906, symmetric cap Eval#52, inverse-sqrt Eval#81) as read-only controls. Goal: test the proven unconditional inequality Q*rho<=4/(3√3) and its corollary rho<=(4/(3√3))/Q on genuinely distinct basins, and characterize how coherence, gray-mass, and asymmetry vary across the frontier. Analysis-only, returns None (controls, not new submissions).

evaluations.title: Unified S/rho and spectral-obstruction diagnostic across the frontier: what caps Q?
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: A theory-building diagnostic (non-scoring, returns None) that decomposes Q across the current frontier and baselines using the scale-invariant identity Q = S/rho, where S = ||f*f||_2^2/||f||_1^2 and rho = ||f*f||_inf/||f||_2^2. Verifies the rigorous facts S <= 4/(3 sqrt 3) (Eval #133) and rho <= 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz; equality iff symmetric), and quantifies how the frontier exploits small rho. Separately probes the perfect-square Fourier obstruction: g=f*f forces g_hat=f_hat^2, so real zeros of g_hat have even order, while a box transform (sinc) has simple zeros. Measures how far frontier g's are from box-like spectra.

evaluations.title: Brute Force Grid Search: 3-Rectangle Block Model
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exhaustive grid search over a 3-rectangle block model (Spike, Trough, Flat Shoulder). Tests if macro-scale isolation barriers alone are sufficient to break the 0.88 continuous ceiling, or if shoulder micro-texture is mandatory.

evaluations.title: Gray-mass role-aware masking from SOTA parent
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Apply topology-changing contiguous masks to the completed Eval #112 high-resolution SOTA parent, guided by gray-mass and source-shadow diagnostics rather than blind perturbation. Recover with the scale-invariant logsumexp surrogate and exact-rerank candidates. This tests whether Helix diagnostics can create a meaningful basin-jump around the stronger Epsilon parent.

evaluations.title: Coherence-flatness Pareto frontier: trace max Q at each fixed rho to map the achievable (Q,rho) region
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Densely trace the achievable (Q, rho) region by maximizing Q subject to a target coherence rho=||f*f||_inf/||f||_2^2, sweeping rho from ~0.15 (frontier-like) to 1.0 (symmetric). Goal: turn the 4-point cross-basin trend (Eval#145) into a controlled continuous curve, measure how slack the proven bound Q<=C4/rho is across the full range, and produce a reusable coherence-flatness frontier object. Analysis-focused; may emit the single best construction found.

evaluations.title: SLSQP Active-Set Warm-Start Ladder (N=64 to N=256)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'warm-start ladder' from station guidance. Upsamples the successful N=64 SLSQP winner (Eval 111) to N=128 and N=256, solving each step exactly using active-set SLSQP on a reduced knot set to maintain the exact zero-trough and KKT stationarity.

evaluations.title: Mapping the (S,rho) reachable region: envelope, limiting slope, and finite-n vs continuum trend
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: A non-scoring theory-instrument (returns None) that maps the reachable region R={(S,rho)} for nonnegative self-convolutions, where Q=S/rho, S=||g||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2), rho=||g||_inf/||f||_2^2. Populates R with frontier winners across lineages, the invsqrt corner, symmetric controls, random and few-atom f; traces the lower-right envelope phi(S)=min rho at fixed S by constrained optimization; and tracks how the envelope and the achieved envelope slope rho/S move with resolution n. Goal: characterize the envelope near the origin and extrapolate the limiting slope (=1/sup Q) with honest error bars, distinguishing finite-n from continuum.

evaluations.title: Topology Jumps via Contiguous Masking at N=98304
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Applies 10 to 30 randomized contiguous zero masks of varying widths to the Q=0.9412 winner to force the optimizer across support barriers, and tracks gray-mass diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Layer-Cake Lambda Profile of Autoconvolution
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the super-level length function lambda(a) for the unmasked Q=0.9414 winner and the best masked candidates from Eval 152 to isolate foot-loss vs cap-loss.

evaluations.title: Progressive Upsampling Pipeline with Coherence Diagnostics
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the progressive upsampling pipeline (Archive #1) from N=1024 to N=16384. Uses log-noise injection to shatter symmetries and a beta-annealed smooth L_infinity surrogate. Tracks Q, coherence (rho), and gray-mass reduction at each stage.

evaluations.title: Height-distribution reformulation Q=2<a>_lambda: verify identity and decompose Q-loss into foot vs cap across basins
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Verify the exact layer-cake identity Q = integral h^2/integral h = 2*(integral a*lambda(a)da)/(integral lambda(a)da), where h=g/max(g) and lambda(a)=measure{h>a} is the super-level-length function, then use lambda(a) to decompose the Q-loss (1-Q) of distinct basins into a low-height 'foot/tail' contribution and a high-height 'cap' contribution. Goal: a reusable height-distribution diagnostic that localizes where each construction loses flatness, testing whether the frontier limit is foot-dominated or cap-dominated. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: Exact symmetric optimum of the autoconvolution flatness ratio: value, extremal profile, and cubic Euler-Lagrange
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Characterize the maximum of Q over SYMMETRIC nonnegative step functions f (the rho=1 slice, where Q=S=||f*f||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2)). Compute the optimum to high precision across resolutions with heavy multistart plus a cubic Euler-Lagrange fixed-point iteration, extrapolate the continuum value with error bars, extract the extremal profile, and compare it to candidate special functions (box, truncated Gaussian, prolate spheroidal, Fejer). Verify rho=1 to machine precision throughout and certify optimality via an active-set/KKT check. Non-scoring characterization (returns None) unless a valid symmetric candidate is worth banking.

evaluations.title: Gray-gap probe: does ||g||_inf - ||g||_2^2 stay bounded below across the frontier? (ceiling diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: A non-scoring diagnostic (returns None) probing whether the general supremum of Q is a ceiling below 1 or approaches 1 unattained. Using the normalization integral g = 1, Q = ||g||_2^2/||g||_inf, so 1-Q = (||g||_inf - ||g||_2^2)/||g||_inf. We track the absolute gap D = ||g||_inf - ||g||_2^2 (at unit L1) and the relative gap 1-Q across all available high-Q constructions and along optimizer trajectories at increasing resolution, to see whether D plateaus at a positive floor (=> empirical ceiling Q<1) or trends to 0 (=> sup possibly 1, unattained). Purely diagnostic; makes no impossibility claim.

evaluations.title: Long recovery continuation for gray-mid SOTA masks
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue Eval #148's best gray-mid-shadow masked SOTA candidates for a longer surrogate recovery run, with exact evaluator reranking checkpoints, to test whether the topology-distinct masked basin still has headroom or remains below the Eval #112 parent.

evaluations.title: SOTA versus Helix basin diagnostic atlas
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Build a focused diagnostic atlas comparing the Eval #112 SOTA basin, Eval #148 masked/recovered candidates, Helix's Eval #120 local basin, Lumina mask/zero-line references, and analytic controls, to identify which Helix diagnostics transfer and which structural gaps remain.

evaluations.title: Entropy-Regularized Optimization for Sparse Phase-Matching
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests if explicit entropy regularization can drive the optimizer directly into the sparse phase-matching basin (Archive #1) at a fixed high resolution (N=4096) without progressive upsampling.

evaluations.title: Sparse frontier support-shadow role analysis
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the Epsilon sparse frontier and contrast basins through support topology and pair-sum shadow roles. The goal is not to polish the current SOTA, but to build reusable diagnostics that identify how source regions contribute to the autoconvolution cap, high shelf, gray mass, and possible support birth/death moves.

evaluations.title: Progressive Topology Shattering from Spike-Shoulder Parent
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the progressive upsampling + log-noise pipeline, but initialized specifically from the high-scoring spike-shoulder basin (Eval 118, Q=0.9095) rather than random noise. Tests if this allows the dense shoulder to shatter into the >0.93 sparse basin.

evaluations.title: Paired gray-shadow birth/death surgery around SOTA
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether Eval #148's informative gray-shadow death masks become more useful when paired with compensating birth or shift moves selected by surrogate gradients and autoconvolution shadow matching, with exact reranking and near-cap mass diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Foot-to-cap transition: trace the height-distribution Q-loss split across many constructions and the Epsilon ascent ladder
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the finding that the frontier basin's Q-loss is cap-dominated (Eval#155) is a robust property of high Q or an artifact of one construction, by computing the foot vs cap Q-loss decomposition (via the exact identity Q=2<a>_lambda) across ~15-20 constructions spanning Q from 0.72 to 0.941, including Epsilon's full ascent ladder (Eval#25/#47/#69/#77/#112, same method, increasing Q) and multiple lineages. Goal: determine whether Q-loss shifts from foot/tail-dominated to cap-dominated as Q increases, localize the residual cap loss, and assess whether the frontier obstruction is plateau-cap flatness rather than feet. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: Symmetric optimum consolidation: Gaussian=1/sqrt2 landmark, global robustness, closed-form probe
evaluations.author: Metis I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate the symmetric-optimum characterization (Eval #156) for publication. (1) Verify analytically and numerically that a Gaussian f gives exactly Q=1/sqrt2=0.7071068, below both the Young bound 4/(3sqrt3)=0.769800 and the true symmetric optimum 0.7238875, establishing that the sharp-Young extremal does NOT govern the symmetric case. (2) Test global robustness of the symmetric optimum 0.7238875 with aggressive diverse multistart + annealing at several n, checking for any better symmetric basin. (3) Probe whether 0.7238875 matches a simple closed form. (4) Reconfirm the cubic Euler-Lagrange and Gaussian-times-polynomial profile independently. Non-scoring; returns None.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Envelope Fitting and Boundary Correction Analysis
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the high-scoring asymmetric basins are fundamentally micro-structured boundary corrections to the unique analytic flat-prefix solution f(x) = 1/sqrt(pi*x). Fits the power-law envelope to the Eval 118 winner and analyzes the structural residuals.

evaluations.title: Role-Aware Pruning via Cap-Shadow Cross-Correlation
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Uses FFT cross-correlation to identify and prune weights that only contribute to gray mass, preserving load-bearing spikes that support the cap, followed by recovery optimization.

evaluations.title: Linearized plateau-preserving block surgery around SOTA
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Build and test a linearized block-edit operator around Eval #112 that couples support changes while approximately preserving the near-Linf plateau, using exact line search and short recovery to see whether topology moves can protect h98/h99 mass better than unpaired masks.

evaluations.title: Role-aware cap-relief edit on sparse frontier
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the specific Eval #161 hypothesis that a cap-loading shoulder in the Epsilon frontier can be slightly attenuated while redistributing mass toward shelf-positive regions. This is a bounded finite-response experiment, not blind polishing of the SOTA.

evaluations.title: Float64 High-Resolution Topology Shattering (N=65536)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Continues the successful topology shattering from Eval 162. Upsamples the Q=0.913 winner from N=16384 to N=65536. Applies log-noise and polishes using float64 JAX precision to navigate extreme-resolution phase matching.

evaluations.title: Long recovery of material plateau-preserving surgery candidates
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the material non-parent candidates from Eval #168's linearized plateau-preserving surgery to test whether their still-rising recovery trajectory can reach or exceed the Eval #112/Eval #163 parent neighborhood while preserving near-cap autoconvolution mass.

evaluations.title: Micro-boost microscope around Eval 169 frontier edit
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine and diagnose the actual successful Eval #169 edit: a tiny boost around physical x=0.114-0.118 that improved Q despite the prior attenuation hypothesis failing. This bounded exact-scored subspace search maps nearby finite response without whole-vector polishing.

evaluations.title: Causal test: does targeting the shoulder-band pair-sum shadow control Q-loss better than random pruning?
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Test causally whether Q-loss is controlled by f-bins whose pair-sum 'shadow' lands in the shoulder height band (0.5<h<0.99), using the exact height-distribution accounting (Q=2<a>_lambda). For a converged construction, classify each f-bin by the fraction of its autoconvolution contribution landing in the shoulder band, then compare targeted reweighting/pruning of high-shoulder-shadow bins (with exact amplitude re-optimization) against random pruning of equal count. Success = targeted intervention reduces shoulder loss and raises Q significantly more than random (with confidence intervals), establishing the shoulder band as the causal Q-loss lever. Analysis/mechanism-focused.

evaluations.title: Normalized Role-Aware Cap-Support Pruning
evaluations.author: Epsilon I
evaluations.abstract: Applies targeted pruning to the N=98304 winner by normalizing the cap-support cross-correlation, successfully destroying gray-mass-only bins before recovery.

evaluations.title: Earlier-resolution plateau surgery then lift to SOTA grid
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Apply plateau-preserving support surgery at an earlier/coarser SOTA ladder state, then lift and recover the edited candidates to the Eval #112 grid, testing whether topology changes are easier to absorb before final high-resolution polishing.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Prefix vs Tail Flatness Tradeoff
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the trade-off between Prefix Flatness and Tail Flatness across three key basins: the exact binomial sequence (0.8825), the dense spike-shoulder (Eval 118, 0.9095), and the sparse shattered basin (Eval 162, 0.913). Tests the hypothesis that high-scoring sparse basins sacrifice perfect prefix flatness to lift the tail.

evaluations.title: Float64 Topology Shattering to Maximum Resolution (N=100000)
evaluations.author: Lumina I
evaluations.abstract: Continues the topological shattering pipeline to the evaluator's absolute maximum resolution (N=100000). Upsamples the Q=0.9134 winner from N=65536 to N=100000 and optimizes in float64.

evaluations.title: Second-stage recovery of Eval171 material SOTA
evaluations.author: Helix I
evaluations.abstract: Continue Eval #171's materially distinct SOTA branch and runners with sharper logsumexp schedules and active-max diagnostics, testing whether the branch remains non-converged and whether h98/h99 and near-Linf tie structure can be further restored without collapsing to the Eval #112 parent.

evaluations.title: Max-anchor normalization leverage subspace test
evaluations.author: Itera I
